why: The answer explains why the inner loop bound must be a[i].length: rows can have different lengths, so a[i].length works for any 2-D array, while a[0].length only works for a regular one such as a 3 × 3 board.

concepts.quote: For a 3 × 3 board I would use a[0].length, but for any 2-D array I need a[i].length.
concepts.why: It correctly uses the length field so the code adapts to each row's real size instead of a fixed size.

concepts.quote: for any 2-D array I need a[i].length
concepts.why: It implies each row is a separate array that may have its own length, which is the ragged-array relation.
It names a[i] as a row but does not apply the indexing rules to the elements.
The answer says nothing about arrays with three or more dimensions.
